description:
On develop 13d4783d0 (seen first on 87aaea64b) this prints [1, 2, :three] on interp and [1, 2, 3] on run and build. Elixir prints [1, 2, :three].

  def pick(3), do: :three
  def pick(n), do: n
  def main() do
    dbg(Enum.to_list(Stream.map([1, 2, 3], &pick/1)))
  end

Measured variants (probes: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-sc8.102-probes/sm_*.fz):
- wrong on run: fn x -> pick(x) end as the mapper; fn x -> case x do 3 -> :three; n -> n end end; atoms ([:a, :b, :c] with pick(:c)); Enum.take/2 over the stream; with pick(3) raising or throwing, run returns [1, 2, 3] and nothing is raised.
- right on run: a guard clause (def pick(n) when n == 3); fn x -> if x == 3 ... end; Enum.map([1, 2, 3], &pick/1); Enum.map over Stream.map(list, fn x -> x end) with &pick/1; a direct pick(3) in the same program.
- fz-lr6 on or off makes no difference (Callables session).

So the miss is a literal pattern matched against the element a stream hands its mapper, in native code only; == on the same element is right. Mechanism not found.

Acceptance: the mechanism is named from an experiment; the program above and the case and raising variants are oracle fixtures on interp, run and build; the full suite passes.

Found while writing the fixture for fz-sc8.102.
title: A literal pattern on a Stream.map element misses on run and build
